ORDERED TO THIRD READING RULES CAL.401

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the labor law, in relation to establishing the warehouse
worker injury reduction program
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S5081

SPONSOR: RAMOS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the labor law, in relation to establishing the warehouse
worker injury reduction program

 
PURPOSE:

Relates to the creation of a program to reduce warehouse workplace inju-
ries via a new section of Labor Law. This bill will support warehouse
workers who currently lack workplace ergonomics standards.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: This Act shall be known as the "warehouse worker injury
reduction program"

Section 2: Amends labor law by adding section XYZ XYZ:

1. Definitions. Provides all definitions.

2. Injury Reduction Program. Each employer shall establish this program
to identify and minimize the risk of musculoskeletal injuries and disor-
ders.

a. Worksite Evaluation. Each job shall have a written work site evalu-
ation by a qualified ergonomist. 1. Evaluation shall include whether
there are quotas in place; 2. Evaluation shall include worker recommen-
dations on risk factors and changes to be made to reduce risk; 3. Copies
of evaluation shall be made available to workers; 4.  Evaluation shall
be conducted within 3 months of effective data and updated annually; 5.
Within 6 months of enactment, the Commissioner shall create standards to
determine certification for qualified ergonomists.

b. Control of risk factors that have caused or are likely to cause
musculoskeletal injuries. Employer shall correct any risk factors iden-
tified in a timely manner. 1. Where eliminating risk cannot be done,
employer shall minimize exposure to risk; 2. To reduce risk factors,
employer shall consider: A. engineering controls and workstation rede-
sign; B.  Administrative controls; C. Records of steps taken to elimi-
nate or reduce risk

c. Training. Employers must provide injury reduction training to employ-
ees, including: 1. Symptoms of musculoskeletal injuries; 2.  Musculosk-
eletal injury risk factors and exposures; 3. Methods to reduce risk
factors; 4. Employer's program to identify risk factors;

5. Rights and functions of Workplace Safety Committees and the right to
report; 6. Unlawful retaliation provisions.

d. Medical Management. Medical professionals operating under legal scope
of practice must staff any on-site medical office or first aid station.
1. Employer must assure such staffing meets New York State requirements;
2. Employers must consult with a NY State-Licensed Physician Board-Cer-
tified in Occupational Medicine if workers must be seen by on-site
medical providers prior to going to doctor; A.  Medical consultant shall
conduct evaluation of on-site medical management program; B. Medical
consultant shall provide a summary of treatment protocols; C. Medical
consultant shall review evaluation annually; D. Designated medical
providers shall observe all jobs in the warehouse; 3. No unnecessary
delays in provision of adequate medical care; 4. No discrimination or
retaliation for reporting work-related injury or illness.

e. Employee Involvement. Employer shall consult employees and designated
representatives to develop and implement all aspects of this program.

3. Unlawful Retaliation.

a. No person shall retaliate against a person for exercising rights
conferred under this act, including; 1. Initiating a request for infor-
mation; 2. Making a complaint related to a quota; 3. Making a complaint
related to Injury Reduction Program.

b. Employee does not need to refer to this Act to be protected.

c. Rebuttable presumption if adverse action taken against a worker with-
in 9 days of engaging in activities protected by this Act. Clear and
convincing evidence must show that, 1. The adverse action was taken for
other permissible reasons; and 2. The activities protected by this act
were not motivating factor in adverse action.

4. Subpoena. Commissioner may request or subpoena employer records and
data upon receipt of complaint regarding a violation of this section.

5. Enforcement.

a. Commissioner of Labor shall enforce this law

b. Inspections. Employees or employee representatives may request an
inspection of a facility.

c. Employer and employee representatives may accompany the commissioner
during an inspection.

d. Commissioner may inspect any aspect of facility where there is reason
to believe a violation exists.

e. Employees accompanying commissioner on inspection shall not lose
wages.

f. Commissioner may conduct inspection upon own initiative.

g. If request for inspection has been made based on imminent danger, the
inspection shall be carried out immediately.

h. If commissioner finds a violation, within 6 months shall issue an
order to comply. Penalties for failure to comply are set.

i. Orders to comply shall be posted at the workplace.

j. Employers and employees may petition the industrial board of appeals
for review of determinations, followed by judicial review.

k. Commissioner can seek judicial enforcement of an order to comply.

l. Injunction proceedings. Where conditions could reasonably be expected
to cause serious physical harm immediately, the Supreme Court has juris-
diction to restrain any practices prohibited under this section.

m. Inspector shall inform employees of any dangers and recommendations
if inspector finds they exist in accordance with subsection 1.

n. If commissioner does not seek relief under this section within 48
hours of notification of such a condition, employees may seek injunctive
relief.

o. Commissioner shall provide a report one year after enactment to the
legislature.

p. If a worksite has annual employee injury rate at least 1.5 times as
high as the warehouse industry average, the commissions shall conduct an
investigation.

q. Commissioner may adopt regulations.

r. If the commissioner brings a successful action to enforce this part,
the court may grant injunctive relief to obtain compliance and shall
award costs and reasonable attorney's fees.

6. Private Right of Action. Employees may bring an action for injunctive
relief to obtain compliance with this Act and may recover costs and
reasonable attorney's fees. Sets limitations on awards.

7. Records. Any records collected based on investigations under this
section shall be made public, although personally identifiable informa-
tion may be protected.

8. Other Powers. The Attorney General may prosecute actions for
violations of this section.

9. Home Rule. No preemption for localities that seek equal or greater
protections under this law.

10. Severability. Provisions are severable.

11. Effective Date. 60 days after it becomes law.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Workplace injuries can take a terrible toll on workers, their families
and their communities, and can create substantial costs for employers.
According to the most recent data (2020) released by the Bureau of Labor
Statistics, the warehouse industry itself reports a rate of serious
work-related injuries involving lost time or restricted duty (4.0
cases/100 full-time workers) that is more than twice the average injury
rates for all private industry (1.7 cases/100 FTE's).The most common
types of work-related serious injury reported by employers in the ware-
house sector are musculoskeletal injuries (MSDs), which often require
workers to miss work and can force workers permanently out of the job
and even out of the workforce.

Warehouse companies often require workers to perform fast paced manual
material handling tasks. These involve well-known risk factors for seri-
ous injury such as rapid pace, repetitive forceful exertions like lift-
ing heavy packages, and awkward postures like twisting/bending, and
combinations thereof that are likely to cause MSDs. Scientific evidence
shows that effective ergonomic interventions --such as reducing the
pace, package weights and stressful postures-- can lower the incidence
and severity of work-related MSDs. The research is clear that the most
effective method for reducing or eliminating these risk factors is to
implement an ergonomics program that includes well-informed analysis of
the worksite, implementation of solutions to reduce the dangerous risk
factors, professionally competent medical management, effective worker
training, and meaningful involvement by workers and their represen-
tatives in all aspects of the program.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

FY 2023: N/A

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect 60 days after it shall become law.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 82 Chapter 652
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 5081-C, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to  amend  the  labor law, in relation to establishing the
        warehouse worker injury reduction program"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This bill seeks to  protect  warehouse  workers  from  musculoskeletal
injuries by requiring employers to establish a worksite injury reduction
program  to  identify and minimize the risk of such disorders that arise
from the fast-paced work and heavy lifting  required  in  the  warehouse
industry.
 
  I  fully support efforts to reduce long term injury and keep warehouse
workers healthy and on the job. However, changes are necessary to permit
a broader class of ergonomics and industrial  hygiene  professionals  to
review  such  worksite  safety  plans due to the lack of board-certified
ergonomists, and to ensure employee-led safety committees are  empowered
to  elevate  their  concerns  regarding ergonomic safety concerns in the
workplace.
 
  I am pleased to have reached an  agreement  with  the  Legislature  to
enact  these  changes.  On  the basis of this agreement, I am pleased to
sign this bill.
 
  This bill is approved.                         (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                                ______

summary: Establishes the warehouse worker injury reduction program; requires employers to establish an injury reduction program designed to identify and minimize the risks of musculoskeletal injuries and disorders among workers involved in performing manual materials handling tasks.
title: Establishes the warehouse worker injury reduction program
